newsitem.title: USA: Maytag returns to profitability, paced by premium brands.
newsitem.headline: Maytag returns to profitability, paced by premium brands.

text.p: Maytag Corp. said Thursday that it returned to profitability last year, paced by its Maytag and Jenn-Air premium brands of appliances.

The manufacturer of home appliances and vending machines said it managed a profit of $136.4 million, or $1.34 a share, last year, despite a $40 million charge for restructuring and $10.5 million in reorganization expenses.
That compared with a loss of $20.5 million, or 19 cents a share, in 1995, when results included $186.8 million in charges or one-time losses.
The company, based in Newton, Iowa, said its sales for the year amounted to $3 billion, about equal to 1995's level, which included $181 million from divested operations.
Sales from ongoing operations, including new businesses, increased 5 percent during 1996, it said.

Maytag, whose brands also include Magic Chef and Admiral, said its profits more than doubled in the fourth quarter, paced by improved sales of appliances, especially its Hoover brand, which posted record results.
The company said its net income for the three months ended Dec. 31 improved to $35.4 million, or 36 cents a share, from $16.6 million, or 16 cents a share.
Revenues for the quarter expanded by 12 percent to $772.9 million from $689.5 million.

The company said its 1996 profits were helped by lower raw material costs and four months of results from its joint venture partner in China, Hefei Rongshida, which is one of that country's leading washing machine manufacturers.
It said its Maytag and Jenn-Air premium brands performed well during the year but value brands were off somewhat.
Maytag also said its sales of refrigeration products were off year-ago levels, due largely to competitive pressures and a sharp decline in private label sales to national customers.
"Our operating performance again was led by the Hoover brand, which posted record results for the year," Chairman Leonard A. Hadley said in a statement.

"The joint venture with RSD in China, which we announced in September 1996, also contributed positively to the corporation's results, and we continue to be very enthusiastic about that business opportunity."

Maytag said, however, that its Dixie-Narco vending equipment manufacturing unit saw sales decline by 17 percent for the year and 24 percent in the quarter as the company encountered production difficulties with a new model.
The company added, however, that it expected Dixie-Narco to improve this year because orders are currently strong and production costs are down from 1996 levels.
Maytag also said it expected its earnings to improve this year, especially in the second half.
It said it will introduce a new refrigerator line in February, a new horizontal washing machine in March and a new Hoover product line in the second half of the year.
Maytag's stock was unchanged at $20 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
